summary.name: Flickbar
summary.one_liner: Flickbar is a free, open-source macOS window manager that snaps, resizes and moves windows with two-finger trackpad gestures on their title bars and Dock icons.
use_cases: Snap a window to a half, third or quarter of the screen
Arrange windows without using the keyboard
Move a window to another display with a gesture
Show, hide or quit app windows from the Dock
Pick a layout from a grid on the title bar
Set up custom gesture and keyboard shortcut mappings
summary.what_it_does: Flickbar lets you swipe two fingers on a window's title bar to snap it to a half, two thirds, a third or a quarter of the screen, fill the screen, or send it to another display. A grid appears when you rest two fingers on a title bar, letting you snap to three-column cells. Swiping on Dock icons shows, hides, cycles or quits an app's windows. Gestures can be remapped in Settings, and keyboard shortcuts can be assigned to actions, none of which are set by default. The page states that Flickbar has no analytics or account, and that update checks are off until enabled.
notable: Two-finger gestures on title bars and Dock icons, with a live highlight preview before the window snaps
Open source under GPL-3.0-or-later; signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple
No analytics or account; update checks off by default
Interface available in English, French and Persian
caveats: Requires a trackpad for gestures; keyboard shortcuts work with any keyboard
Pinch and double-tap gestures need Zoom and Smart zoom enabled in macOS trackpad settings
